content_metadata.description: The video explores the creation of the Vessel, an iconic structure designed by Thomas Heatherwick, detailing its design and construction process, and the vision behind it.

qAndA.answer: Vessel was engineered at Cimolai in Monfalcone, Italy.

qAndA.answer: He wants to create things that are unique, meaningful, and different from anything else in the world.
qAndA.question: What is Thomas Heatherwick's design philosophy?

qAndA.answer: He envisions Vessel as a free and accessible space for everyone to enjoy, offering a new kind of landmark for New York City.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: We all want to do something good. We all do. We've tried to start by thinking of what's the best thing you could do.
Trying to see how we can make something that feels particular that doesn't exist anywhere else in the world.
It is very hard to know when something's finished and I will keep trying to make something the best it can be, the best it can be because that's my passion.
There are some things that are universal about us.
Humans need places to have their own spirit and personality.
The crossmanship of this project is really, I think, exceptional.
So when I was just walking up now, I was just enjoying the obvious pride that the team have built it.
The crossmen who have made this project in New York, in Italy,
and all sorts of places that have all come together.
Behind me is a phenomenal piece of making.
Our hope is to make a different kind of public experience.
It's free for everybody that is a sort of one of the little landmarks we have in our lives.
I can't wait till there are people streaming up here.

youtube_description: Thomas Heatherwick explains the intent and experience of Vessel, a new New York monument designed by Heatherwick Studios.
